Fix the MEDIUM and LOW findings from the customer-journey rehearsal of the Nxeon hosting platform at /opt/nxeon. They are documented in `docs/QA-JOURNEY.md` — read the MEDIUM and LOW sections in full. Verify each against the current source before changing it.

The set, in the doc's own numbering: M1 (Deploy button greyed out with no explanation), M2 (dashboard and server page scroll sideways at 390px — traced in-browser to grid tracks, NOT the tables everyone suspects), M4 ("Get Started Free" is not true and onboarding walks people into the wall), M5 (the footer promises "All systems operational" on every page, unconditionally), M6 (four different, contradictory support-response promises), M8 (forms that lose long free text), M9 (the cookie banner blocks the chat and feedback buttons), M10 (portal mobile drawer: no Escape, no accessible name, stays in the tab order), M11 ("Coming soon" shipped on the billing page — note another agent may already have addressed this when wiring the card UI, so CHECK before acting), M12 (empty states that point at nothing), M13 (seven public CTAs dump logged-out visitors at a login wall with no way back), plus everything under LOW.

Two of these are truth problems rather than polish, and matter most:
- **M5** — a footer that claims "All systems operational" without consulting anything is the same defect as a migration reporting success it never verified. Either read real status or do not make the claim.
- **M4 and M6** — copy that promises something the product does not do. Fix the product or fix the promise; do not leave a customer to discover the gap.

Design rules: match the existing design system exactly — read neighbouring components and reuse their tokens, spacing and component vocabulary rather than inventing any. The user has been explicit that everything must match the Nxeon theme. Write copy from the customer's side of the screen: name things by what people recognise, say exactly what a control will do, and make every error explain what went wrong AND how to fix it. An empty state must say what to do next.

For M2 specifically: the horizontal scroll was traced to grid tracks. Wide content (tables, code, diagrams) should scroll inside its own `overflow-x: auto` container so the page body never scrolls sideways — but find the actual offending tracks rather than wrapping things at random, and verify the fix at 390px. Note the sidebar was recently made fixed on both portals and the rehearsal found no overlap at any width, so do not regress that.

VERIFY, reporting only what you observed:
- `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit ; echo "exit=$?"` — must be 0.
- `cd /opt/nxeon && npm test` — currently 174/174, must stay green.
- `cd /opt/nxeon && npx next build` to prove the pages compile. IMPORTANT: `nxeon-web.service` serves production directly from `/opt/nxeon/.next`, so a build in place would swap live customers onto un-reviewed code. Build in a throwaway copy instead (hardlink the tree, symlink `node_modules`, exclude `.env`), as a previous agent did successfully.
- Exercise the real pages against STAGING (`nxeon-staging-web`, port 3001) in a browser at 390px and at desktop width. Say plainly which findings you RAN versus only READ.

Do NOT edit: `lib/actions.ts`, `components/AuthForms.tsx`, `lib/order.ts`, `lib/proration.ts`, `lib/renewal-quote.ts`, `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts`, `app/api/stripe/**`, `worker/**`, `components/customer/PaymentMethod.tsx`, `docs/QA-JOURNEY.md`, `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` — other agents own those this round. `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx` is shared, so touch it only for M11 and only if it is genuinely still unfixed. Do not deploy, restart production services, or commit.

Report: each finding with its verdict (fixed / already fixed / not reproducible), what you RAN versus READ, screenshots or measurements for the mobile work, and anything you chose to leave.

1	# QA — Full customer journey rehearsal
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-07-26
4	**Environment driven:** staging (`nxeon-staging-web` :3001, nginx :8080 / `https://staging.nxeon.cloud`, DB `nxeon_staging`, `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`)
5	**Production touched:** read-only `GET` on public marketing pages only. No Stripe charge, no VM create/destroy, no DNS/OVH change, no outbound mail to a real person.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 0. Method, and a caveat that affects how you read this
10	
11	Every finding below is tagged:
12	
13	- **[RAN]** — I drove it over real HTTP/a real browser and watched it happen.
14	- **[READ]** — I traced the code path and did not execute it. Never presented as an observed result.
15	
16	Test accounts created on staging: `dana.quill2@example.com`, `sam.card@example.com`, `sam.two@example.com`. Six sandbox servers and ~$1,500 of play money. All disposable.
17	
18	### Caveat: staging is 21 commits behind production
19	
20	`/opt/nxeon-staging` is at `8c8b7d9`; `/opt/nxeon` is at `fd71056`. Twenty-one commits apart, including several that touch exactly what I was asked to test (wallet floor, proration symmetry, Stripe-provision coupling, coupons, notification prefs, sidebar).
21	
22	So for **every** finding I observed on staging I diffed the responsible file against the production tree and said which applies. Where the file is byte-identical I say so explicitly. **This staleness is itself a launch-readiness problem**: the environment built to rehearse the release does not contain the release. Re-run `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` before trusting staging for anything else.
23	
24	---
25	
26	## LAUNCH BLOCKERS
27	
28	### B1. The wizard charges the customer when they click "Continue →", four steps before the confirmation screen
29	
30	**[RAN]** — reproduced 5 times, 5 servers created, 5 wallet debits.
31	`components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:646-661` — **byte-identical in staging and production.**
32	
33	On the **Access** step, type a valid hostname and click **Continue →**. Instead of advancing to Review, the order is placed immediately: a `Next-Action` POST to `payAndDeploy`, wallet debited, VM provisioned, browser redirected to the new server's page.
34	
35	The customer never sees the Review step. They never choose a billing term (it commits at the `default_term`, currently Monthly). They never see "Due today". There is no confirmation of any kind between clicking a button labelled *Continue* and money leaving their wallet.
36	
37	Verified ledger from one such click:
38	
39	```
40	-629  Order: Starter VPS (qa-probe-02) — Monthly · Summer Sale 30% off first term
41	```
42	
43	**Root cause** (**[READ]**, following from the observed behaviour): the two buttons are branches of an unkeyed ternary in the same DOM position.
44	
45	```jsx
46	{!isLast ? (
47	  <button type="button" ... onClick={() => setStep((s) => s + 1)}>Continue →</button>
48	) : (
49	  <button className="btn-primary px-6" disabled={pending || !canDeploy} ...>   // no type → submit
50	)}
51	```
52	
53	React reconciles both branches onto the **same `<button>` element** and patches its attributes. `setStep` runs inside the click handler, React re-renders synchronously, and `type="button"` is removed from the very node the browser is still processing the click for. The browser then performs its default action — submit. It only fires when `canDeploy` is true, which is why an **empty** hostname reaches Review correctly and a **filled** one does not. That is the whole bug.
54	
55	- Wallet-funded customer: **charged with no confirmation screen.**
56	- Zero-balance card customer **[RAN]**: `payAndDeploy` returns a `checkoutUrl`, but the redirect is gated on `submittedRef` which the Deploy button never got to set — so the redirect is suppressed and the customer lands on Review looking normal. No charge, no visible damage, but a stray Stripe Checkout session per traversal.
57	
58	**Smallest fix:** add distinct `key` props (`key="continue"` / `key="deploy"`) so React unmounts one and mounts the other, and give the deploy button an explicit `type="submit"`.
59	
60	---
61	
62	### B2. "Renew now (+30 days, $8.99)" charged $97.09 and added 12 months
63	
64	**[RAN]** — clicked it, watched the debit and the date move.
65	`components/SubscriptionControls.tsx:35,90` (display) vs `lib/actions.ts:629-654` (charge). **`SubscriptionControls.tsx` is byte-identical in staging and production.**
66	
67	On a Starter server bought on an annual term:
68	
69	| | |
70	|---|---|
71	| Button label | `Renew now (+30 days, $8.99)` |
72	| Confirmation dialog | **none** — one click, immediate debit |
73	| Actual charge | **$97.09** (`-9709` in `WalletTransaction`) |
74	| Paid-until before | 2027-07-26 |
75	| Paid-until after | **2028-07-26** |
76	
77	The card is handed `server.plan.priceCents` — a **monthly** figure — and hardcodes the string "+30 days", while `renewNow` prices `vpsTermPriceCents(plan.priceCents, server.termMonths)` and advances `addMonths(base, term.months)`.
78	
79	A **10.8×** overcharge here. On Max/36-month it is `$32.99` shown against `$950.11` charged — **28.8×**. No dialog, no undo.
80	
81	**Smallest fix:** `lib/stripe-cards.ts:124` already exports `renewalCharge(server, prices)` — the exact function `worker/billing.ts` renews with. Compute it in `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`, pass `{totalCents, months}` into `RenewalCard`, and build the label from those. Add a confirm dialog stating the amount.
82	
83	---
84	
85	### B3. The site-wide promo bar advertises a price no plan has — live on production right now
86	
87	**[RAN]** — fetched `https://nxeon.cloud/` and `/pricing`.
88	`components/marketing/PromoBar.tsx:19` — `const exampleRegular = 500;`
89	
90	Every marketing page carries:
91	
92	> Summer Sale · **30% off your first term** — VPS from ~~$5~~ **$3.50/mo**, renews at $5/mo.
93	
94	The cheapest active plan is **Starter $8.99 → $6.29**. There is no $5 plan; the only sub-$8.99 row in the DB is `nano`, and it is `active = false`. So the headline number is **80% below** anything purchasable, and the same page renders the real grid a few hundred pixels lower — the contradiction is visible in one screenshot.
95	
96	The comment directly above the constant claims the opposite of what the code does: *"show the honest first-term price so the bar's headline number matches what checkout charges."*
97	
98	**Smallest fix:** derive it — `const exampleRegular = Math.min(...activePlans.map(p => p.priceCents))` — or delete the "from $X" clause and keep only the percentage.
99	
100	---
101	
102	### B4. There is no email verification anywhere in the product
103	
104	**[RAN]** — registered `dana.quill2@example.com`, was signed in and on `/dashboard` immediately.
105	`lib/actions.ts:115-139`; **no `emailVerified` field and no verification-token model exist in `prisma/schema.prisma`.**
106	
107	`register()` creates the user, calls `createSession()`, best-effort sends a welcome email, and redirects to `/dashboard`. Anyone can sign up with **any** address, including one they do not control, and immediately transact.
108	
109	For a hosting business this is the account-recovery and abuse-control foundation: signup-credit and referral farming across throwaway addresses (`grantSignupCredit` / `maybeRewardReferral` both fire on an unverified account), and a mistyped address means invoices, root passwords and dunning notices go to a stranger with no way to recover.
110	
111	**Smallest fix:** ship a `User.emailVerifiedAt` + token table, gate *ordering* (not login) on it, and reuse the existing `PasswordResetToken` mail plumbing.
112	
113	---
114	
115	## HIGH — money and trust
116	
117	### H1. The term cards state a recurring price that will never be charged
118	
119	**[RAN]** — read verbatim off the running Review step.
120	`components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:544-563`
121	
122	```
123	−10%  Annual   $5.66/mo   $67.96 billed every 1 yr
124	−20%  Triennial $5.03/mo  $181.24 billed every 3 yr
125	```
126	
127	"$67.96 billed every 1 yr" is the **promo first-term** price. Renewals bill the regular price — `$97.09` — which I confirmed by actually renewing (B2). `currentPromo()` never returns null (`LAUNCH_SALE`, 15%, `lib/promotions.ts:58-65`), so this is wrong on **100% of orders, 100% of the time**.
128	
129	The disclosure below it — *"30% off your first term applied — renews at the regular price"* — carries no number and no date, and the strikethrough regular total appears only on the "Due today" row, not on the card that says *billed every*.
130	
131	`components/marketing/PricingGrid.tsx:110` gets this exactly right (*"First term. Renews at $8.99/mo."*). Copy that.
132	
133	**Smallest fix:** `{money(total)} first term · renews at {money(regTotal)}` — `regTotal` is already in scope at line 544.
134	
135	### H2. Stripe order confirm re-prices after the card is charged and takes the difference from the wallet
136	
137	**[READ]** — `lib/actions.ts:391-430` → `lib/stripe.ts:41` → `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts:70-80` → `lib/order.ts:158,188,197`
138	
139	The Checkout session metadata carries the *intent*, never the quoted total, so `placeOrder` re-runs `orderQuote` at confirm time — including a fresh `currentPromo(new Date())`. If the promo rotates between checkout creation and the Stripe redirect, the recomputed total is debited from the wallet with no new consent. With no balance: payment captured, no server, and a notification reading *"Payment received — we couldn't finish setting up your server."*
140	
141	This is an inconsistency rather than an oversight in principle: `lib/resize.ts:115` and `lib/disk-expand.ts:153` already take the amount from Stripe metadata precisely so confirm cannot re-price. The order path is the one that missed it.
142	
143	**Smallest fix:** add `c: quote.chargeCents` to the `nxeonOrder` metadata and give `placeOrder` an optional `chargeCents` override, mirroring `applyResize`.
144	
145	### H3. A card-paid purchase produces two PAID invoices and doubles "Paid · lifetime"
146	
147	**[READ]** — `lib/stripe.ts:230-239`, `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts:70`, `app/dashboard/invoices/page.tsx:23-25,38`
148	
149	`creditCheckoutSession` writes a PAID *"Wallet top-up"* invoice for every paid session, then the order branch writes its own. An $82.53 annual purchase shows as `Wallet top-up $82.53` + `Starter VPS — Annual $82.53`, and the invoices page reports **$165.06** paid lifetime.
150	
151	Each document is internally consistent (`lib/invoices.ts:139-163` derives totals from line items), so nothing is fabricated — but a customer reconciling against their card statement sees twice their spend. `worker/billing.ts:615-617` already states the correct rule for the renewal path.
152	
153	**[RAN] counter-check:** for **wallet-paid** orders and renewals the invoices reconcile *exactly* with the ledger — 7 invoices, 7 wallet rows, amounts identical including the $97.09 renewal. The defect is specific to the Stripe leg.
154	
155	### H4. Automatic backups can silently never exist while the UI shows a fresh timestamp every night
156	
157	**[READ]** — `worker/backup-schedule.ts:55-61`, `worker/index.ts:745-768,979-985`; customer-facing at `components/customer/BackupSchedule.tsx:103-105`
158	
159	`lastAutoBackup` is stamped **when the job row is enqueued**, not when the backup succeeds — and it is written nowhere else. `backupCreate` gates the vzdump task's exit status but never checks the archive exists or is non-zero, has no failure notification, and is excluded from `VM_STATE_FAILURE_JOBS`.
160	
161	So "Last automatic backup: 2026-07-26 04:00 UTC" means *a row was created*. vzdump could have failed every night for a month with no alert, and the schedule is marked satisfied so the retry is a full interval away. Discovered at restore time — the one moment it cannot be fixed.
162	
163	Aggravating: the deploy wizard **sells** this at the point of sale (**[RAN]** — Add-ons step reads *"Daily auto-backups · Included · Nightly snapshots to separate storage for easy restore"*).
164	
165	**Smallest fix:** drop the `lastAutoBackup` write in `backup-schedule.ts` (the in-flight de-dupe at :50-53 already prevents pile-up) and set it in `backupCreate` after a storage-content read shows a fresh volid with `size > 0`. Add a failure `notify`.
166	
167	### H5. `syncPortForwards` flushes the whole NAT chain and rebuilds it unverified
168	
169	**[READ]** — `worker/network.ts:28-55`
170	
171	Line 30 unconditionally runs `iptables -t nat -F NXEON_FWD`, then rebuilds per-server in a loop with no try/catch, no rollback and no `-C` read-back. `exec` here is `promisify(execFile)`, so **one** failed `-A` rejects and aborts the loop — every server after that point is left with no DNAT rule. #!/bin/bash
# Deploy a ref (default: main from /opt/nxeon) to the staging environment.
# Usage: ./scripts/deploy-staging.sh [git-ref]
set -euo pipefail
REF="${1:-main}"
cd /opt/nxeon-staging

echo "==> Syncing staging to $REF"
git fetch origin
git reset --hard "origin/$REF"

echo "==> Installing dependencies"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -1

echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss 2>&1 | tail -2
npm run db:seed 2>&1 | tail -2 || true

echo "==> Building"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4

# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. Only .next needs to be writable by
# it (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable, and systemd
# injects .env as root. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon-staging/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon-staging/.env 2>/dev/null || true

echo "==> Restarting staging services"
systemctl restart nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
echo "==> Staging responds: HTTP $CODE (http://$(grep ^PUBLIC_IP .env | cut -d= -f2):8080)"
[ "$CODE" = "200" ] || { echo "STAGING UNHEALTHY"; exit 1; }
echo "==> Staging deploy complete"
